chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: He (peace be upon him) pointed thereby to the Chief of the Negroes.

key_terms.الشَّرِيفُ: The Sayyid (referring to Sharif al-Radi, the compiler of Nahj al-Balagha)
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الزَّنْجِ: The Chief of the Negroes (Ali ibn Muhammad, leader of the Zanj Rebellion)

ai.seo_question: Who is Sahib al-Zanj referred to in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi identifies this reference as pointing to Ali ibn Muhammad, the leader of the Zanj Rebellion, whose uprising in Basra (869–883 CE) fulfilled the Imam's prophecy regarding the region's instability. This connection highlights the historical accuracy attributed to the Imams in Shia tradition, linking their spiritual insight to specific socio-political upheavals in the Abbasid era.
